paragraphs: Friend, this poem is about love, and it isn't shy about it. The man looks at the young woman and he doesn't hold back. He calls her beautiful, and he says it from her feet all the way up to her tresses (Song of Solomon 7:1-5). God put that in His Word on purpose, so love between a husband and wife is something to treasure, not something to be embarrassed about.

Now look at what the young woman does with all that praise. She doesn't just soak it in. She says, "I belong to my beloved, and his desire is for me" (Song of Solomon 7:10). Then she invites him out to the countryside, and she says she has treasured up "every delicacy, new as well as old" for him (Song of Solomon 7:13). That is love that gives. It belongs to someone, it plans, and it saves the best for the one it belongs to.

Then she closes with a charge to the daughters of Jerusalem: "Do not arouse or awaken love until the time is right" (Song of Solomon 8:4). I think that's the heart of it, baker. Love is a good gift, and good gifts are worth waiting for. Slow down, trust God's timing, and let love come when it's ready, because it's worth more than any batch I've ever pulled out of the oven. The Song of Songs isn't finished with this thought yet, so keep baking.
